signals.headline: France and Spain fires force more than 300,000 to flee homes
signals.summary: In France, around 50,000 people were evacuated from their homes overnight into Sunday, according to interior minister Laurent Nuñez.
keyTakeaways: Firefighters spray water in a burning forest near Lacanau, southwestern France, Saturday, July 25, 2026.
Devastating wildfires in Spain and France have forced more than 300,000 people to evacuate their homes.
The most devastating fires are in the Southwest, in the Gironde and Landes regions, French President Emmanuel Macron said on social media Saturday.
signals.whyItMatters: Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska has declared a national state of emergency because of the wildfires.

ja.headline: 仏・西で大規模山火事、30万人超が避難
ja.summary: フランスとスペインを襲った山火事により、30万人以上が自宅からの避難を余儀なくされた。フランスでは日曜未明にかけて約5万人が避難したと、ローラン・ニュニェス内相が明らかにした。
keyTakeaways: フランス南西部ラカノー近郊の森林で、消防隊員が延焼する炎に放水を続けた
スペインとフランスで猛威を振るう山火事により、30万人超が避難を強いられている
最も深刻な被害はジロンドおよびランド地方に集中しているとマクロン大統領が土曜日にSNSで述べた
ja.whyItMatters: スペインではフェルナンド・グランデ＝マルラスカ内相が山火事を受けて国家非常事態を宣言した。

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: And what about Spain?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Spain's situation is serious enough that their interior minister declared a national state of emergency because of the wildfires.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: They're working on it, but the scale is challenging. French President Macron posted about the fires on social media Saturday, calling them devastating.

captions.text: It sounds like both countries are really struggling right now.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: They are. With over 300,000 people displaced, it's one of the larger wildfire emergencies we've seen in that region.

captions.speaker: narrator

captions.speaker: narrator

captions.speaker: narrator

captions.text: 森林火災は夏の乾燥と高温で起きやすく、今回は広い範囲に影響が出ています。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 避難した人々の多くは、いつ自宅に戻れるか見通せない状態です。

signals.headline: RFK Jr urges Alzheimer’s screening but blunts key panel that could drive research
signals.summary: The US health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr, has called for better Alzheimer’s screening – but a critical federal panel that might have helped researchers find practical ways to do that has been prevented from meeting for more than a year.
keyTakeaways: The panel, formally called the US Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF), had planned to issue a recommendation on screening for cognitive decline this year, alongside 13 other topics as varied as autism screening and food allergy prevention.
The Trump administration has prevented the taskforce from meeting since March 2025, a political appointee fired two panel chairs, and the administration has so far failed to appoint new members.
The USPSTF recommendations can help inform future research, said Ruiz, as their draft recommendations are open for public comment and frequently receive substantial input from research communities.
signals.whyItMatters: There is no major treatment for Alzheimer’s.

ja.headline: アルツハイマー対策を訴えながら、研究を支える委員会を空洞化
ja.summary: 米国のケネディ厚生長官はアルツハイマー病の早期スクリーニング強化を訴えている。しかし、その実現に向けた具体的な指針を担うはずだった連邦諮問委員会は、一年以上にわたって開催を阻まれたままだ。
keyTakeaways: 米国予防サービス作業部会（USPSTF）は今年、認知機能低下のスクリーニングに関する勧告を、自閉症や食物アレルギー予防など十三のテーマとともに公表する予定だった。
トランプ政権は二〇二五年三月以降、同委員会の開催を停止。政治任用者が委員長二名を解任し、後任の選定も進んでいない。
USPSTFの勧告案は広く公開され、研究者コミュニティからの意見を集める場にもなっていた。その機能が失われつつある。
ja.whyItMatters: アルツハイマー病には、いまだ有効な治療法がない。

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: I saw that RFK Junior is calling for better Alzheimer's screening. That sounds like a good thing, right?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: It does on the surface. But there's a federal panel that helps figure out how to actually do that kind of screening, and it hasn't been allowed to meet for more than a year.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Wait, what panel?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: It's called the US Preventive Services Task Force. They were planning to issue a recommendation on screening for cognitive decline this year, along with thirteen other health topics.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So the administration stopped them from meeting?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Yes. The Trump administration has prevented the taskforce from meeting since March twenty twenty-five. A political appointee also fired two panel chairs, and no new members have been appointed.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Why does this panel matter so much?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Their recommendations help inform future research. They release draft recommendations for public comment, and research communities weigh in. It's part of how we figure out what works.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: And there's still no major treatment for Alzheimer's?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: That's right. Which is why the research and screening questions feel especially important.

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: アメリカでは、アルツハイマー病の早期発見を進めようという声が政府から上がっています。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: ケネディ厚生長官が、もっと積極的にスクリーニングを行うべきだと訴えているのです。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: ところが、その方法を具体的に示す役割を担う連邦の委員会が、一年以上開かれていません。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: この委員会は、認知機能の検査をどう進めるかといった指針を出す予定でした。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 政権が委員長を解任し、後任も決めないまま活動を止めてしまったのです。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: この委員会の勧告案は、研究者が意見を寄せる場でもありました。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: アルツハイマー病には、まだ決定的な治療法がありません。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 対策を掲げながら、それを支える仕組みが動かない状況が続いています。

signals.headline: Samsung Galaxy Unpacked 2026: The 6 biggest announcements
signals.summary: Samsung’s annual summer event kicked off on Wednesday morning with the company unveiling a new lineup of watches and foldables.
keyTakeaways: If you weren’t able to watch the event yourself, you can catch up with all of this year’s biggest Galaxy Unpacked announcements below.
The new Fold also features an updated hinge design with Samsung’s new Flex Titanium display tech.
It doesn’t completely eliminate the crease on the inside display, but it does make it significantly less noticeable than the crease on Samsung’s previous foldables.
signals.whyItMatters: The highlight of Galaxy Unpacked was the Galaxy Z Fold 8, which got a major redesign from last year’s Z Fold 7.

ja.headline: サムスンが折りたたみスマートフォンと新型ウォッチを発表
ja.summary: サムスンは夏恒例の発表イベント「Galaxy Unpacked」を水曜朝に開催し、新世代の折りたたみ端末とスマートウォッチのラインアップを公開した。
keyTakeaways: 発表内容はすべて後からまとめて確認できる
新型Foldはヒンジを刷新し、独自のFlex Titaniumディスプレイ技術を採用
内側の折り目は完全には消えないものの、従来モデルと比べて目立ちにくくなった
ja.whyItMatters: 今回の目玉はGalaxy Z Fold 8で、前世代のZ Fold 7から大幅にデザインが刷新された。

signals.headline: Corporate America may be using AI to cut jobs, but small businesses are using it to keep them
signals.summary: Last year, most small businesses were using AI to get answers to questions, review contracts, create policies and rewrite emails.
keyTakeaways: It is exhausted owners using technology to help scarce employees do more work, make fewer mistakes and serve more customers.
There are almost 7.6m job openings this month, an increase from pre-Covid levels and most predominantly at small businesses.
Robot technology – even if a smaller company could afford them – is years away from installing dishwashers, fixing HVAC systems, laying pipes and putting up drywall.
signals.whyItMatters: Gusto says that small businesses are expected to hire about 974,000 recent grads ages 20 to 24 in the 2026 season, up from 962,000 in 2025.

ja.headline: 大企業がAIで雇用を削る一方、中小企業はAIで雇用を守る
ja.summary: 昨年、多くの中小企業がAIを活用し始めた。契約書の確認、社内規定の整備、メールの文章改善など、日常業務の効率化が主な用途だ。
keyTakeaways: 疲弊した経営者たちが、限られたスタッフでより多くをこなすためにAIを頼っている
今月の求人数は約760万件と、コロナ禍以前を上回り、その多くは中小企業からの募集
食洗機の設置や配管工事、内装作業をこなせるロボットの実用化は、費用面の問題以前に、まだ数年先の話だ
ja.whyItMatters: 人事サービスのGustoによると、中小企業が2026年シーズンに採用する見込みの20〜24歳の新卒者は約97万4千人と、2025年の96万2千人から増加する見通しだ。

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So I keep hearing about AI taking jobs, but this story seems to say something different is happening with small businesses?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Right. While bigger companies might be cutting positions, small businesses are actually using AI to help their existing employees do more work and make fewer mistakes.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: What are they actually using it for?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Last year, most were using it for pretty practical things – getting answers to questions, reviewing contracts, creating policies, rewriting emails. The everyday stuff that takes time.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Is this because they can't find enough workers?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Exactly. There are about seven point six million job openings right now, which is actually higher than before Covid. And most of those openings are at small businesses.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So it's not really about replacing people with robots?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Not at all. The physical work small businesses do – installing dishwashers, fixing heating systems, laying pipes, putting up drywall – robot technology for that is years away. And most smaller companies couldn't afford it anyway.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Are they planning to hire more people?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Yes. Small businesses are expected to hire about nine hundred seventy-four thousand recent grads this year, up from nine hundred sixty-two thousand last year.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So AI is more like a helper than a replacement for them.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: That's the picture here. Exhausted owners using technology so their scarce employees can serve more customers.

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: アメリカでは大手企業がAIを使って人員削減を進める一方で、中小企業は逆に人手を守るためにAIを使い始めています。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 昨年、多くの中小企業が契約書の確認やメール文の作成といった日常業務にAIを取り入れました。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 疲れ切った経営者たちが、少ない従業員でより多くの仕事をこなせるよう、技術に頼っているのです。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 今月の求人数は約760万件で、コロナ禍前より増えており、その大半が中小企業からの募集です。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 配管工事や内装作業をこなせるロボットは、費用以前に実用化まで数年かかる見通しです。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 人事サービスのGustoによれば。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 中小企業が2026年に採用する20代前半の新卒者は約97万人と、前年から増える見込みです。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 人手不足が続く中、中小企業にとってAIは人を減らす道具ではなく、人を支える道具になっています。

signals.headline: Nasa boss praises rise of women in science
signals.summary: The head of science at Nasa has praised the "fantastic" rise of women in science.
keyTakeaways: The 57-year-old graduated from university with a masters in telematics and satellite engineering in 1991 and was one of only four women on the course of more than 200 students.
The scientist explained she had grown up unaware a passion for science was "unusual" for girls.

She had attended St Francis College, an all-girls school in Letchworth, which she said shielded her from the gender stereotypes that often discourages young women from studying science, technology, engineering and mathematics (Stem).
signals.whyItMatters: Dr Nicola Fox, who grew up in Hitchin, Hertfordshire, said she had been struck by the number of women now graduating in physics and engineering when she returned to the University of Surrey.

ja.headline: NASAの科学部門トップ、理工系に進む女性の増加を歓迎
ja.summary: NASAの科学部門を率いる責任者が、科学分野における女性の躍進を「素晴らしい変化だ」と称えた。
keyTakeaways: 1991年、200人以上が在籍するテレマティクス・衛星工学の修士課程を修了した際、女性はわずか4人だった。
幼い頃、科学への関心が女子にとって「珍しいこと」だという意識はなく、自然にその道を歩んできた。
女子校出身だったことで、理系分野から女性を遠ざけがちな性別による固定観念とは無縁に育った。
ja.whyItMatters: サリー大学を訪れた際、物理や工学を修める女性の数が大きく増えていることに深く心を動かされたという。

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: I saw Nasa's head of science was talking about women in science. What's the story?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Dr. Nicola Fox, who leads science at Nasa, recently praised what she called the fantastic rise of women in the field.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: What made her notice this change?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: She went back to the University of Surrey and was struck by how many women are now graduating in physics and engineering. That's very different from her own experience.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: How different was it back then?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: When she graduated with a masters in telematics and satellite engineering in 1991, she was one of only four women in a class of more than 200 students.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: That's quite a contrast. Did she say what helped her pursue science?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: She grew up unaware that a passion for science was considered unusual for girls. She went to an all-girls school in Letchworth, which she said shielded her from gender stereotypes that often discourage young women from studying science and engineering.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So she just followed her interests without those barriers.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Exactly. And now she's seeing that shift happening more broadly, with many more women entering these fields.

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: NASAで科学部門を統括するニコラ・フォックス博士が、理工系に進む女性の増加を目にして、大きな変化を感じています。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 博士自身は1991年に衛星工学の修士課程を終えましたが、200人を超える学生のうち女性はわずか4人でした。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 彼女が育った環境は少し特別で、女子校に通っていたため、科学が女性に向かないという偏見に触れずに済みました。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: そのおかげで、科学への興味を持つことが珍しいとは思わず、自然にその道を選んだそうです。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 最近、母校のサリー大学を訪れた博士は、物理や工学を学ぶ女性が大幅に増えていることに驚きました。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: この変化は、若い世代が性別にとらわれず、自分の関心を追いかけられる時代になってきた証しかもしれません。
